title: Microconsumption Ledger: export-first view for per-token/per-message charge breakdown
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype a compact, export-first ‘Microconsumption Ledger’ in the Redwood Console that surfaces token-level and message-level cost decomposition across routes, models, and time. The view should allow engineers and finance users to: 1) toggle resolution (per-token, per-message, per-session), 2) inspect amortized vs raw token costs, 3) attribute cost to model variant + route + customer tag, and 4) build CSV/Parquet exports with selectable columns and time rollups. This ticket is focused on UX patterns, export builder interactions, and a small interaction spec for handling very large result sets without overwhelming the UI or export pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma prototype with three ledger modes: 'Raw tokens', 'Amortized cost', and 'Attribution view'
Export builder mock that supports column selection, time-rollup (hour/day/auto), and output formats (CSV/Parquet)
Interaction spec for progressive loading, server-side aggregation fallback, and CSV sampling policy when rows > 1M
Design tokens and spacing/redlines for table, filters, and compact rows delivered in handoff file
Design walkthrough recorded and sign-off from PM and one backend engineer
Accessibility checklist passed (keyboard nav for table, column headers with aria-sort, color contrast for cost deltas)
comments: 2026-02-16 Maya: Initial exploration sketch attached. Goal is to keep default ledger rows compact (single-line per event) with expandable detail pane for provenance and prompt snippets.
2026-02-22 Arjun (PM): Prefer amortized-per-session as default for finance users — but keep raw-token toggle for debugging. Add a small helper tooltip explaining amortization assumptions.

2026-02-28 Eng review (R. Singh): Backend can provide per-token deltas but we should limit default API to aggregated rows to avoid very large responses. Proposed solution: server-side rollup endpoint + preview sampling endpoint for 'Export > Show sample'

2026-03-03 Design review (Lena): Reduced column density suggestion — move less-used columns into an 'expand' details panel. Re-ordered columns to: timestamp, route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, billable_tokens, unit_price, cost, attribution_tags.

2026-03-08 Finance feedback (C. Morales): Need a rate-card mapping column to show which pricing slab applied per row for reconciliation. Also request for a 'rebill reason' column when discounts/commits applied.
2026-03-11 UX QA (J. Park): Keyboard focus order verified on prototype; remaining: implement aria-live for export job status and ensure color for negative deltas meets contrast.
2026-03-12 Lena: Preparing final handoff bundle. Removed inline sample query to avoid leaking internal IDs; using sample-dashboard link instead. Ready for eng handoff meeting on 2026-03-15.
design_decisions: Default mode = 'Amortized cost' to surface predictable billing for finance/product teams, with toggle to 'Raw tokens' for debugflows
Compact single-line rows with an expandable detail tray to reduce cognitive load and improve scanability
Export builder first: surface a WYSIWYG column selector and pre-defined templates (Billing CSV, Audit CSV, Analytics Pivot) to cover common use cases
Use server-side rollups by default and preview sampling for exports when dataset cardinality is large
Include a 'Rate card' column that maps each row to the applied pricing slab (SKU id) to simplify downstream reconciliation
risks_and_mitigation: Large volumes: mitigate with server-side aggregation, cursor-based pagination, and sampled export previews
Cost confusion: show tooltip explaining amortization, and link to rate-card docs for edge cases
Performance of export job: suggest background export jobs with email/console notifications for > 30s exports
Privacy: redact prompt text in default exports; include 'include_prompts' toggle gated behind role/permission
handoff_notes: Deliver Figma pages with exported CSS token file and redlines
Provide example API payloads for rollup endpoints and export semantics in Confluence
List of required backend metrics: billable_tokens, cached_tokens, model_variant, sku_id, discount_applied
Suggested story split for ENG: 1) rollup endpoint + small UI, 2) export builder + background job, 3) detail tray + accessibility refinements
